rounds.text: Amal Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a robust rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 with a medium confidence BUY rating [E53]. The company boasts exceptional profitability and capital efficiency, with a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 26.0% [E6] and a return on equity (ROE) of 20.4% [E7], easily outperforming the sector median ROCE of 10.5% [E64]. Top-line expansion has been blistering, highlighted by a compounded sales growth rate of 78% over the trailing twelve months [E10] and a 5-year historical profit growth of 21.0% CAGR [E51]. Furthermore, the business is completely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E29], and its profits are fully backed by cash with a 1.00x cash conversion ratio yielding ₹ 22 Cr in operating cash flow [E25, E26]. Operating within a supportive sector tailwind score of +0.76 [E59], a discounted cash flow model indicates intrinsic value sits at ₹ 989 per share against a market price of ₹ 748, offering a 24.4% margin of safety [E35, E36]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed in recent periods (-4 percentage points in TTM and -7 percentage points in the June 2026 quarter) alongside volatile raw material prices for sulphur [E21, E22, E75].

Despite the prevailing optimism, Amal Ltd carries substantial operational and valuation risks that are clearly highlighted in the underlying record. The company is facing severe and immediate contractions in profitability, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth plunging to -22% [E13]. Furthermore, operational margins are eroding rapidly; the TTM operating margin has fallen by 4 percentage points to 14% [E21], while the quarterly operating margin experienced an even sharper drop of 7 percentage points down to 18% in June 2026 compared to the same period a year ago [E22]. Compounding this margin compression is the inherent vulnerability of monthly price volatility in sulfur, its key raw material, which serves as a persistent operational cost headwind [E75]. From a valuation and market perspective, the stock trades at an expensive price-to-book multiple of 7.68x [E2], reflecting rich pricing that leaves little margin for operational missteps, especially given its historical extreme volatility and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -84.9% [E43]. Conceded: the company operates with zero debt [E29], has a low 1-year implied growth rate from reverse DCF metrics [E37], and exhibits strong short-term sales growth [E54]. However, these favorable financial conditions do not insulate the business from its sharp recent profit declines and margin degradation.

The bear exaggerates immediate contractions by ignoring that the broader picture remains fundamentally robust, backed by a rule-based screen score of 90 out of 100 [E53]. Conceded: TTM profit growth is -22% [E13] and operating margins have compressed in recent periods [E21, E22]. However, this cyclical noise masks an elite underlying return profile, including an ROCE of 26.0% and an ROE of 20.4% [E6, E7], both comfortably outperforming the sector median ROCE of 10.5% [E64]. The rich price-to-book ratio of 7.68x [E2] is entirely justified by a pristine, zero-debt balance sheet [E29], full cash conversion of 1.00x where profits are completely backed by cash [E25], and positive free cash flow of Rs 15 Cr [E27]. Finally, the bear's fear of historical drawdowns [E43] is neutralized by current momentum, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40] and sitting inside a strong chemical sector tailwind score of +0.76 [E61].

Conceded: rule-based screen score is 90 out of 100 [E53]. However, the bull attempts to dismiss TTM profit contraction of -22% [E13] and operating margin compression—dropping from 18% to 14% over three years [E21] and falling by 7 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E22]—as mere cyclical noise, yet offers no evidence that these margin headwinds have stopped eroding profitability. While the bull touts an ROCE of 26.0% and ROE of 20.4% [E6, E7], it glosses over the fact that the 5-year median ROE sits at a modest 11% [E18], indicating that recent high returns are a cyclical peak rather than a durable baseline. Conceded: the balance sheet has zero debt [E29] and positive free cash flow of Rs 15 Cr [E27]. Even so, a price-to-book multiple of 7.68x [E2] leaves little margin for error when raw material volatility in sulfur presents an ongoing operational cost headwind [E75] and past performance features a severe historical drawdown of -84.9% [E43] alongside an annualized volatility of 71.9% [E44]. Finally, pointing to moving averages [E40] fails to counteract a 12-month share price return of -24.3% [E42], showing that recent momentum offers cold comfort to shareholders facing persistent downward pressure.

Conceded: TTM profit growth is -22% [E13], annual operating margin compressed by 4 percentage points over three years [E21], and quarterly margin fell 7 percentage points [E22]. However, the bear's dismissal of returns as a cyclical peak ignores that both the 3-year median ROE and the last year's median ROE stand robustly at 20.0% [E19, E20], demonstrating multi-year structural improvement well above the 5-year median of 11% [E18]. Furthermore, the bear ignores that sales growth remains exceptionally strong across 5-year (51%), 3-year (58%), and TTM (78%) horizons [E8, E9, E10], vastly outperforming the sector median sales growth of 15.3% [E63]. Conceded: annualised volatility is 71.9% [E44] and the historical drawdown reached -84.9% [E43]. Nonetheless, the company commands a relative-strength rating of 99 against the Nifty 500 alongside positive moving average alignment [E40, E41], proving that current market strength directly contradicts the bear's claim of persistent downward pressure.

Conceded: 3-year and 1-year median ROE stand at 20.0% [E19, E20]. However, the bull's reliance on these figures ignores the 5-year median ROE of just 11% [E18], confirming that the recent profitability is a volatile cyclical peak rather than a durable structural baseline. Conceded: sales growth over 5-year (51%), 3-year (58%), and trailing twelve month (78%) horizons outpaces the sector median of 15.3% [E8, E9, E10, E63]. Nevertheless, this rapid top-line expansion has failed to translate into bottom-line gains, as evidenced by a trailing twelve month profit contraction of -22% [E13]. Conceded: the relative-strength rating is 99 with positive moving average alignment [E40, E41]. Yet technical strength cannot override fundamental margin degradation, given that quarterly operating margins dropped by 7 percentage points to 18% [E22] and annual operating margins compressed by 4 percentage points to 14% [E21], while the stock itself carries a severe annualised volatility of 71.9% [E44] and a devastating historical drawdown of -84.9% [E43].
